1.
Challenge in this petition is made to the removal order dated 20.09.2005.
The petitioner was an employee of the respondent Vadodara Municipal Corporation.
For proved misconduct in departmental inquiry, he is imposed major punishment of removal from service vide order dated 20.09.2005.
Appeal against the said order is also rejected by the Appellate Authority vide order dated 10.11.2005.
It is this removal which is questioned in this petition.

2.1 The petitioner, who appeared in person, has addressed the Court almost for the whole days on 08.09.2017, HC-NIC Page 1 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER 09.06.2017 and 12.06.2017.
This aspect is noted by this Court, in the orders of the respective dates.

sentences.text: This Court (Coram: Hon'ble Ms.Justice Sonia Gokani) had, vide order dated 27.03.2017 requested Ms.Rina Kamani, learned advocate to assist the Court in this matter on behalf of the petitioner, for the reasons recorded therein.
Pursuant to the said order, Ms. Rina Kamani, learned advocate has appeared in this matter and she has also addressed this Court on behalf of the petitioner.
2.3 Mr.Parth Bhatt, learned advocate has appeared and addressed this Court on behalf of the respondent Corporation.
2.4 Mr.Rashesh Rindani, learned Assistant Government Pleader appeared on behalf of the State Authorities, which are formal respondents.

3. Though the petitioner has raised various grievances, the subject matter of this petition, as noted above is, the order dated 20.09.2005 whereby the petitioner is removed from service of the Corporation as Junior Clerk and therefore the legality of the said order is only examined in this petition.
4. It is noted that though the petitioner has addressed the Court at length for days, no specific contention is raised with regard to the impugned order dated 20.09.2005.
His entire thrust was on the point that, he ought to have been continued as Food Inspector and not as Junior Clerk.
That aspect is already concluded in the earlier round of litigation, reference to which is made hereinafter.

Suffice it to note that, the HC-NIC Page 2 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER petitioner has not made any specific submission with regard to the impugned removal order dated 20.09.2005.

5. Ms.Rina Kamani, learned advocate has also taken this Court through the material on record to attempt to point out, as to how the petitioner is aggrieved by the various actions of the respondent Corporation.
Since there is no specific contention with regard to the impugned order dated 20.09.2005, even Ms.Kamani, learned advocate has not been able to show any specific point in that regard.
6. Mr.Parth Bhatt, learned advocate for the respondent Corporation has drawn the attention of this Court to two affidavits in reply.
One is dated 29.01.2011 and the second is dated 08.09.2016.
This Court has taken into consideration the contents thereof.

7. Having heard the petitioner in person, Ms.Kamani, learned advocate (for the petitioner),
Mr.Bhatt, learned advocate for the respondent - Corporation and having considered the material on record, this Court finds as under.
7.1
So far the impugned order dated 20.09.2005 is concerned, the petitioner was served with the charge sheet dated 21.10.2003.
The same is on record at page:1877 to 1880.

It was for not resuming duty as Junior Clerk, though, not only his Appointing Authority had passed order to that effect, but the same was confirmed by this Court vide order dated 24.02.2006 in Special Civil Application No.6665 of 2001.

sentences.text: Pursuant to the said charge sheet, Departmental Inquiry HC-NIC Page 3 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER was conducted in the prescribed procedure.
7.3 There was insistence on the part of the petitioner that he should be continued on the post of Food Inspector and not as Junior Clerk.
He did not report for duty for years together on the post of Junior Clerk and under these circumstances, ultimately, inquiry was conducted, concluded and he was removed from the service.
There is ample material on record which indicates that sufficient opportunity was given to the petitioner.
This Court further finds that the inquiry is not vitiated either in procedure or in substance.
There is neither any material nor any contention to the contrary.
7.4 This Court does not find any infirmity in the impugned order dated 20.09.2005 passed by the Disciplinary Authority.
7.5 The said removal order was challenged in appeal.
The said appeal was considered by the appropriate Authority and the same was dismissed vide order dated 10.11.2005.
7.6 Considering the totality, this Court finds that there is no illegality / infirmity in the removal order dated 20.09.2005 which is confirmed by the Appellate Authority vide order dated 10.11.2005.
No interference therefore is required in that regard.
This petition, therefore would be required to be dismissed.
8. The following further facts need to be noted.
8.1 The date of birth of the petitioner is 13.04.1953.
Had he continued in service, he would have retired on 30.04.2011 on HC-NIC Page 4 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER attaining the age of superannuation.
8.2 He had initially joined the service with the respondent Corporation as Junior Clerk in November, 1974.
8.3 He was subsequently appointed as a Food Inspector by the respondent Corporation in May, 1995 for a specified period.
On expiry of the said period, the petitioner was asked to work as Junior Clerk.
He was not ready for that.
8.4 The petitioner has taken this Court through the hundreds of papers.
His principal grievance is that he ought to have been continued as Food Inspector and not as Junior Clerk.

On this point only,
litigation is going on since more than two decades.
8.5 Though there are number of orders passed by this Court, reference needs to be made to few of them, which are as under.

sentences.text: The present petitioner had earlier filed a petition being Special Civil Application No.750 of 1998.

The said petition was disposed of by the Division Bench of this Court (Coram :
Hon'ble the Chief Justice Mr.Justice D.M.Dharmadhikari and Hon'ble Mr.Justice M.S.Shah) vide order dated 20.12.2000 in the following terms "1. This petition is filed by Dineshkumar Mohanlal Sheth contending that he is entitled to be posted as a Food Inspector and has challenged the letter/order dated 5.1.1998 HC-NIC Page 5 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER (Annexure "A" to the petition) issued by the Deputy Municipal Commissioner (Admn.) of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation calling upon the petitioner to perform the work of only Junior Clerk and not to work as a Food Inspector.

There was no interim relief in favour of the petitioner and still the petitioner did not discharge the duties of a Junior Clerk for a long period and, therefore, the Corporation has initiated a departmental inquiry against the petitioner and has suspended him from service for disobedience of the orders of the superior authorities and for unauthorized absence.

The departmental inquiry is pending against him on the ground that even though he was asked to perform the work of only Junior Clerk,
he was taking the samples under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has thus committed serious misconduct.

2. In view of the finding recorded by us in the judgment delivery today in Special Civil Application Nos. 1917/91 and cognate petitions that the post of Food Inspector is not a substantive post as such, but an employee of a local authority is to be designated as a Food Inspector by notifying his name as a Food Inspector in the official gazette, it cannot be said that the petitioner was substantively appointed as a Food Inspector.

In any view of the matter, as far as the present petition is HC-NIC Page 6 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER concerned, it appears that he is facing a departmental inquiry.

We see no reason to entertain this petition when the petitioner has no substantive right to work as a Food Inspector as it is within the domain of the local authority to decide as to which of its employees notified as Foods Inspectors in the official gazette are to be assigned duties of Food Inspectors.

3. As far as the communication dated 5.1.1998 is concerned, we do not find any fault with the same as the Corporation has pointed out that the petitioner could not be assigned the duties of a Food Inspector when no such workload was available with the Corporation.
4. We dispose of this petition without going into the merits of the charges levelled against the petitioner which shall be duly adjudicated in the departmental enquiry.

Such inquiry shall be disposed of as expeditiously as possible and preferably within three months from the date of receipt of the writ of this Court or a certified copy of this order, whichever is earlier.

The present petitioner had filed Special Civil Application No.6665 of 2001.
Against non grant of interim relief in the said petition, he had preferred Letters Patent Appeal No.1191 of 2001.
The said appeal was dismissed by the Division Bench of this Court (Coram: Hon'ble Mr.Justice M.S.Shah and Hon'ble Mr.Justice D.A.Mehta) vide order dated 07.11.2001 in the following terms.

"1. In this appeal, the original petitioner has challenged the order passed by the learned Single Judge admitting the petition i.e. Special Civil Application No.6665 of 2001 but not granting any interim relief as prayed for by the petitioner.
The order of the learned Single Judge does not indicate whether the petitioner had pressed for the interim relief.
In any case, looking to the interim relief prayed for in terms of prayer clause 10(A), such a relief cannot be granted at this stage.
Hence the appeal deserves to be dismissed summarily.

2. The appellant who appears as a party in person however submits that if the interim relief as prayed for is not granted, the appellant will be required to join as a Junior Clerk and all his rights and contentions raised in the main petition are likely to be prejudiced if he resumes duty as a Junior Clerk.
HC-NIC Page 8 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:

We, therefore, dismiss this appeal with a clarification that it will be open to the appellant to resume duty as a Junior Clerk without prejudice to his rights and contentions raised in Special Civil Application No.6665 of 2001.
It will also be open to the appellant to move the learned Single Judge for fixing an early date of final hearing.
4. Subject to the aforesaid observations, the appeal is dismissed.
5. Since the appeal is dismissed, the civil application does not survive and is accordingly dismissed."

sentences.text: The petitioner thereafter moved Civil Application No. 10232 of 2005 challenging the order of removal dated 20.09.2005 passed by the Municipal Commissioner, Vadodara Municipal Corporation.

Accordingly, the main matter and Civil Application No. 10232 of 2005 were heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment and order.

25. After having heard the petitioner as party-in-person and Mr. Pranav G. Desai, learned advocate appearing for the respondent - Corporation and after having gone through the entire previous record of this case and various proceedings initiated by or against the petitioner before this Court and various orders passed in those proceedings and petitions as well as Letters Patent Appeals and after having gone through the relevant Rules, Acts, statutory provisions and service rules pertaining to the issues raised before the Court, the Court is of the view that there HC-NIC Page 11 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER is no dispute about the fact that the petitioner was initially appointed as Food Inspector.
However, that appointment was subject to certain conditions, more particularly, the appointment was initially for a period of six months.
It was subject to the pending departmental inquiry and it was also subject to issuance of the notification by the State Government.

Once the period of six months was over, even this Court has not granted any relief to the petitioner and challenge raised against not continuing the petitioner as Food Inspector was rejected by this Court on the ground that the period of six months was over.
It is true that the State Government has issued Notification only after the contempt proceedings were filed and pursuant thereto, the petitioner has found his place in the said Notification.

However, initially because of the stay granted by the lower Court and thereafter the stand was taken by the respondent - Corporation that there was no vacancy for the post of Food Inspector and as and when the vacancy arises, the directions will be issued to promote the petitioner to the post of Food Inspector.

Despite the fact that the petitioner's appointment as food Inspector was not made and despite the fact that this Court has also passed several orders directing the petitioner to work as Junior Clerk without prejudice to his rights and HC-NIC Page 12 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER contentions raised in the petition, the petitioner has not accepted the work of Junior Clerk and he did not resume on duty.

Once the Division Bench of this Court has held that the post of Food Inspector is not a substantive post and the petitioner cannot be appointed on that post since he was already holding a substantive post as a Junior Clerk, there is no other option for the respondent - Corporation but to reinstate the petitioner as Junior Clerk.

All these contentions which have been raised by the petitioner with regard to his right to be appointed as Food Inspector fell into insignificance in view of the binding decision given by the Division Bench of this Court and based on that, the petitioner's petition was also disposed of by this Court.

If the petitioner has any grievance,
the petitioner should have taken the order of the Division Bench before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
But the respondent authority and even this Court is bound by the decision of the Division Bench and the petitioner has to work as a Junior Clerk.

The petitioner has pointed out that the order of Division Bench is challenged before the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Special Leave Petitions were admitted and stay is granted against the implementation and operation of the order.

There was no interim relief in favour of the petitioner and still the petitioner did not discharge the duties of a Junior Clerk for a long period and, therefore, the Corporation has initiated a departmental inquiry against the petitioner and has suspended him from service for disobedience of the orders of the superior authorities and for unauthorized absence.
The departmental inquiry is pending against him on the ground that even though he was asked to perform the work of only Junior Clerk,
he was taking the samples under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and has thus committed serious misconduct.
2. In view of the finding recorded by us in the judgment delivery today in Special Civil Application Nos. 1917/91 and cognate petitions that the post of Food Inspector is not a substantive post as such, but an employee of a local authority is to be designated as a Food Inspector by notifying his name as a Food Inspector in the official gazette, it cannot be said that the petitioner was substantively appointed as a Food Inspector.
In any view of the matter, as far as the present petition is HC-NIC Page 6 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER concerned, it appears that he is facing a departmental inquiry.
It was subject to the pending departmental inquiry and it was also subject to issuance of the notification by the State Government.
Once the period of six months was over, even this Court has not granted any relief to the petitioner and challenge raised against not continuing the petitioner as Food Inspector was rejected by this Court on the ground that the period of six months was over.
It is true that the State Government has issued Notification only after the contempt proceedings were filed and pursuant thereto, the petitioner has found his place in the said Notification.
However, initially because of the stay granted by the lower Court and thereafter the stand was taken by the respondent - Corporation that there was no vacancy for the post of Food Inspector and as and when the vacancy arises, the directions will be issued to promote the petitioner to the post of Food Inspector.
Despite the fact that the petitioner's appointment as food Inspector was not made and despite the fact that this Court has also passed several orders directing the petitioner to work as Junior Clerk without prejudice to his rights and HC-NIC Page 12 of 23 Created On Thu Jun 15 00:13:53 IST 2017 C/SCA/19748/2007 CAV ORDER contentions raised in the petition, the petitioner has not accepted the work of Junior Clerk and he did not resume on duty.
Once the Division Bench of this Court has held that the post of Food Inspector is not a substantive post and the petitioner cannot be appointed on that post since he was already holding a substantive post as a Junior Clerk, there is no other option for the respondent - Corporation but to reinstate the petitioner as Junior Clerk.
If the petitioner has any grievance,
the petitioner should have taken the order of the Division Bench before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
But the respondent authority and even this Court is bound by the decision of the Division Bench and the petitioner has to work as a Junior Clerk.
Despite specific order passed by the respondent - Corporation, the petitioner has not even worked as a Junior Clerk and ultimately his services were terminated and he was removed as a Junior Clerk from the service of the respondent - Corporation which order is challenged in Civil Application No. 10232 of 2005.
26.
